title: Nested Decisions and Decision Trees
learningObjectives: Explain how one decision can contain another decision.
Trace nested if/else structures and identify which inner block is reached.
Represent nested decisions as a simple decision tree.
Avoid ambiguous else placement by using braces and indentation.
Refactor overly deep nesting when a clearer structure is possible.

understand.concept: A nested decision is an if or else structure placed inside another decision's branch. The outer condition determines which section of code is reached; then an inner condition can make a more specific choice. A decision tree is a diagram of these possible paths.
understand.whyItMatters: Some decisions depend on more than one level of eligibility or state. For example, a user may first qualify as a member, then receive a different offer based on purchase amount. Nested decisions model such dependent choices.
understand.analogy: At a venue, the first check asks whether a visitor has a ticket. Only ticket holders go to the next check for seat type. Each check opens a smaller decision.
understand.analogyLimit: Real programs may have many possible paths and conditions that change over time. A tree is a simplification; always trace actual code and validate the conditions.

explain.narrative: Nested decisions place a second if/else inside an outer branch. The inner condition is evaluated only when execution reaches it. Indent clearly and use braces to make each else belong to its intended if. Draw a decision tree to list paths, and consider reducing deep nesting with early returns, helper functions, or a multi-branch chain when appropriate.

examples.title: Member then purchase threshold
examples.explanation: The outer condition selects the member path; the inner condition then checks the purchase total.

examples.title: Nested path when outer condition is false
examples.explanation: Because the outer condition is false, the inner if is never reached.

examples.title: Two levels of access checks
examples.explanation: The outer login check passes; the inner admin check chooses the user dashboard.

examples.title: Trace a nested discount
examples.explanation: The outer age branch is selected, then the inner accompanied check is true.

examples.title: Simplify a deep choice
examples.explanation: Nested branches represent dependent checks. For more complex structures, a decision tree or helper function may make the paths easier to understand.

commonMistakes: Misplacing else so it binds to an unexpected if.
Ignoring the inner condition because only the outer condition was traced.
Excessive nesting that hides the path logic.
Not testing each path, including the false path of the outer condition.

guidedTask.title: Guided: Membership reward decision
guidedTask.instructions: First check membership. If the person is a member, check whether the purchase total is at least 1000 and print the appropriate member reward. Otherwise print the guest message.
steps: Inside the member branch, add the purchase threshold decision.
Indent and brace both levels carefully.
Test member and guest paths plus both inner outcomes.

independentTask.title: Independent: Account access decision tree
independentTask.instructions: Model access decisions: if signed out, show Sign in; if signed in but not verified, show Verify account; if verified but not admin, show User dashboard; if verified admin, show Admin dashboard. Create a decision tree sketch before coding.
requirements: Use at least one nested decision.
Ensure inner conditions are evaluated only on the relevant outer path.
Make every outcome reachable and distinct.
Use braces and indentation to clarify else ownership.

hints: An inner condition runs only if its containing branch is selected.
Indent inner branches one level deeper and use braces.
Sketch a tree to enumerate all possible paths.
Test the false branch of every outer decision.
If nesting becomes deep, consider simplifying or extracting a helper.

questions.answer: A decision placed inside another decision branch
questions.explanation: Nested decisions perform a more specific check after an outer branch has been selected.

questions.prompt: When does an inner if condition execute?
options: Only when execution reaches its containing outer branch
Only when the outer condition is false
questions.answer: Only when execution reaches its containing outer branch
questions.explanation: The outer condition controls whether the nested block is reached.

questions.prompt: What can a decision tree help you do?
questions.explanation: A tree maps conditions and outcomes so paths can be checked.

questions.prompt: What makes nested if/else code easier to read?
questions.explanation: Clear indentation and braces help identify which else belongs to which if.

questions.prompt: What should you consider if nesting becomes very deep?
options: Simplify the structure or extract helper functions
questions.answer: Simplify the structure or extract helper functions
questions.explanation: Refactoring can reduce complexity and make decision paths easier to maintain.
